Plot a variation partitioning

Source: R/plot_varpart.r
plot.ecodive_varpart.Rd

A Venn diagram of varpart()'s result: a circle (or, for four sets, an ellipse) for each set of variables, with the adjusted \(R^2\) of each fraction in its region, and that of the residuals below.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_varpart'
plot(x, digits = 2L, col = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

The result of varpart().

digits

The number of decimal places of the fractions. Default 2.

col

The sets' colours, one per set. Defaults to grDevices::hcl.colors()'s "Dark 3" palette.

...

Passed on to graphics::plot.default(), such as main, sub or cex.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The regions are all the same size, whatever their fractions: their values are written in them, not drawn to scale. Fractions shared by several sets can be negative, when the sets explain more together than the sum of what they explain apart. The fractions are the adj_r_squared column of x, and its row names ([a], [b], ...) follow the regions as in vegan::showvarparts(): [a] is the first set's own fraction, [b] the second's, and so on.

Examples

    vp <- varpart(
      iris[, 3:4], species = ~ Species, sepal = ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width,
      data = iris, norm = 'hellinger' )
    plot(vp)


    vp <- varpart(
      iris[, 3:4], species = ~ Species, length = ~ Sepal.Length,
      width = ~ Sepal.Width, data = iris, norm = 'hellinger' )
    plot(vp)
